concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 15 September 2026
justifications: The DPA sets a maximum of 48 hours after awareness of a personal data breach. The amendment reducing this to 24 hours does not take effect until 1 October 2026.

concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amendment effective 1 October 2026 replaces the breach-notification deadline with a maximum of 24 hours. The later operational amendment does not take effect until 1 March 2027.

concepts.name: Audit notice period in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amendment effective 1 October 2026 reduces the on-site audit notice period to 20 days. The audit protocol's 10-Business-Day provision conflicts with the amendment's main body, which takes precedence over its annex.

concepts.name: Liability cap in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: Amendment No. 1 took effect on 1 October 2026 and replaced the prior liability clause with a EUR 1,000,000 cap for breaches of the DPA. The cap is fixed, so the EUR 700,000 in fees does not change it; confidentiality breaches are excluded from the cap.

concepts.name: Liability cap covers confidentiality breaches
justifications: Effective 1 October 2026, Amendment No. 1 states that the Processor's liability cap does not apply to breaches of the DPA's confidentiality section.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 November 2026
justifications: Meridian Mail Ltd is listed as an approved Sub-processor in Annex 3. Its approval is withdrawn only with effect from 1 January 2027, so it remains approved on 1 November 2026.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 February 2027
justifications: The amendment withdraws Meridian Mail Ltd’s approval effective 1 January 2027, so it was not an approved Sub-processor on 1 February 2027.

concepts.name: Distinct data locations count as of 1 February 2027
justifications: As of 1 February 2027, personal data locations include Norway and Estonia, plus Lithuania, France, and Denmark through the approved sub-processors. Ireland is excluded because Meridian Mail's approval was withdrawn effective 1 January 2027.

concepts.name: Deletion deadline for year-end termination
justifications: The amendment effective 1 October 2026 reduced the deletion period from 90 to 60 days. Sixty days after termination on 31 December 2026 is 1 March 2027.

concepts.name: Breach notification obligation summary
predicted: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay, and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting data processed under the dpa. the notice must describe the breach’s nature, the categories and approximate numbers of affected data subjects and records, likely consequences, and measures taken or proposed to address and mitigate it.
gold: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and within 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting data processed under the dpa, describing its nature, affected categories and approximate numbers of data subjects and records, likely consequences, and measures taken or proposed to address the breach and mitigate its effects. it must document all breaches and cooperate with any regulatory notifications or data subject communications the controller determines are required.
values: The Processor must notify the Controller without undue delay, and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach affecting data processed under the DPA. The notice must describe the breach’s nature, the categories and approximate numbers of affected Data Subjects and records, likely consequences, and measures taken or proposed to address and mitigate it.
justifications: The amendment effective 1 October 2026 reduces the notification deadline to 24 hours, while the DPA’s notification-content requirements remain unchanged.

concepts.name: Applicable initial notification regime
justifications: Usable privileged credentials were confirmed exposed, so the expedited 12-hour limit applies from the original awareness of the breach, which occurred when unauthorized access was verified.

concepts.name: Initial notice lateness in minutes
justifications: Verified unauthorised access established awareness at 17:10 on 9 April, and the later-confirmed usable credential exposure makes the 12-hour limit run from that original awareness. The deadline was 05:10 on 10 April, while the first notice arrived at 06:00.

concepts.name: Completed follow-up report deadline
justifications: Awareness occurred on 9 April, which is excluded from the count. The third counted Business Day is 16 April after excluding the 12 April closure and the Controller-approved pause on 14 April.

concepts.name: Held ORD records deletion deadline
justifications: The ordinary deletion deadline is 60 calendar days after the 30 June 2027 termination, or 29 August 2027. The last hold ends on 25 August, and the tenth Business Day after release is 9 September 2027, which is later and therefore controls.

concepts.name: BK-0630 deletion deadline
justifications: The backup contains no held records, so it is due by the earlier of its ordinary deletion deadline and 35 calendar days after creation. The 35-day deadline from 30 June 2027 is 4 August 2027, earlier than the ordinary 60-day deadline.

concepts.name: Permitted uses of held ORD records on 1 September 2027
justifications: The last hold ended on 25 August, but the records remain within the post-release deletion window on 1 September. During post-termination retention under the hold and its deletion window, use is limited to legal preservation, not service delivery or analytics.

concepts.name: Nordlicht infrastructure approval start
justifications: Approval could begin only after the proposed start date, written consent, and security review were all in place. The security review completed on 22 April 2027, the latest of these conditions.

concepts.name: Ordinary customer email providers on 10 May 2027
justifications: Cendrillon Mail SAS was approved to provide transactional email and is stated to continue ordinary transactional email. Meridian's temporary emergency permission explicitly did not restore ordinary customer email, while no consent was recorded for the proposed Finland email service.

concepts.name: Authorised data locations on 15 May 2027
justifications: Personal Data processing and effective authorisation are established for Norway, Estonia, Lithuania, and France through continuing approved services. Sweden also qualifies: processing began after the proposed start date, security review, and written Controller consent were all in place; the other listed countries either lack required authorisation or processing, or their permission had expired or been withdrawn.

concepts.name: Written consent date for Nordlicht email in Finland
Security cap before earlier payments in EUR
justifications: Qualifying fees are EUR 1,140,000 after excluding VAT and subtracting the EUR 60,000 credit; the one-off training fee and fees for the event month are excluded. Twice that amount, EUR 2,280,000, exceeds the EUR 2,000,000 floor for the security cap.

concepts.name: Ordinary cap remaining before new claims in EUR
justifications: The ordinary cap is EUR 1,000,000 per Contract Year, and EUR 300,000 has already been paid for ordinary breaches in LC-27’s Contract Year, leaving EUR 700,000.

concepts.name: Total payable on new claims in EUR
justifications: Qualifying fees are EUR 1,140,000 after excluding VAT, the credit, training, and April fees, making the security cap EUR 2,280,000; after the EUR 500,000 same-year payment, EUR 1,780,000 remains, sufficient for the EUR 1,750,000 shared security loss. The ordinary claim receives EUR 700,000 after the prior ordinary payment, while the two confidentiality losses are uncapped, for a total payable of EUR 2,800,000.
